2609.02285.title: Entangled Representations Amplify Collateral Damage in Unlearning
2609.02285.paper_summary: A long-held intuition in interpretability research is that representational entanglement, the sharing of structure between knowledge domains in a neural network, makes unlearning harder. While the intuition is widespread, it has never been directly tested in a controlled experiment. We present a way to do so: by repurposing Selective Gradient Masking (SGTM), we train a suite of six 254M-parameter language models on English Wikipedia with graded levels of disentanglement between biology and non-biology knowledge. Applying three standard unlearning methods to every model in the suite, we find that more disentangled models consistently achieve better retain-forget trade-offs: at a fixed level of forgetting, the most disentangled models incur roughly $4\times$ lower retain cost under two of the three methods, and $1.3\times$ lower under the third. Because our intervention changes only the model, not the data or the unlearning algorithm, this is direct evidence that representational entanglement is one of the causes of collateral damage in unlearning, as interpretability researchers have long suspected. A similar design could be used to test other structural claims from interpretability.
2609.02285.paper_summary_zh: 一個長期存在於可解釋性研究中的直覺是，表示的糾纏，即神經網絡中知識領域之間結構的共享，使得去學習變得更加困難。雖然這一直覺廣泛存在，但從未在控制實驗中直接測試過。我們提出了一種方法：通過重新利用選擇性梯度遮罩（SGTM），我們在英語維基百科上訓練了一套六個254M參數的語言模型，並在生物學與非生物學知識之間進行了不同程度的解糾纏。對每個模型應用三種標準的去學習方法，我們發現，更加解糾纏的模型在保留與遺忘的權衡上始終表現更佳：在固定的遺忘水平下，最解糾纏的模型在三種方法中的兩種下，保留成本約低$4\times$，在第三種方法下低$1.3\times$。因為我們的干預只改變了模型，而不是數據或去學習算法，這直接證據表明表示的糾纏是去學習中附帶損害的原因之一，正如可解釋性研究者長期以來所懷疑的。類似的設計可以用來測試可解釋性中的其他結構性主張。
